status_summary: Executive Order 14173 revoked EO 11246 on 2025-01-21, and DOL ordered OFCCP to stop investigations and enforcement under that order on 2025-01-24. On 2026-08-21 DOL published three final rules: one rescinds the EO 11246 regulations (effective 2026-10-26, after today's date), and two narrow the Section 503 and VEVRAA rules (mostly effective 2026-09-21). OFCCP itself still exists and enforces Section 503 and VEVRAA; the administration's FY2026 budget proposal to end its funding was not adopted, and Congress cleared about $100 million for it in February 2026.

timeline.event: President signs EO 14173, which revokes EO 11246 (the order that created OFCCP's contractor affirmative-action and nondiscrimination regime). The order was published in the Federal Register on 2025-01-31.

Secretary's Order 03-2025 directs OFCCP to cease investigative and enforcement activity under EO 11246 and places Section 503 and VEVRAA activity in abeyance. Contractors were told to wind down EO 11246 compliance by 2025-04-21. OFCCP later administratively closed pending compliance reviews.

DOL/OFCCP publish proposed rules to rescind the EO 11246 regulations and to revise the Section 503 and VEVRAA regulations. Comments were due 2025-09-02 and the deadline was later extended; the final rule notice reports 917 comments on the rescission proposal.

Secretary's Order 08-2025 lifts the abeyance on Section 503 and VEVRAA enforcement (date per a law-firm summary); the EO 11246 provisions of Order 03-2025 remain in force. A DOL page states Section 503 and VEVRAA and their regulations remain in effect.

Congress clears the FY2026 spending bill funding OFCCP at roughly $100 million (about $11 million below the prior year). The White House had proposed ending its funding and moving remaining functions to EEOC and DOL's veterans office.

OFCCP publishes three final rules. The EO 11246 rescission removes the order's regulations in 41 CFR chapter 60 (parts 60-1 through 60-4, 60-20, 60-40, 60-50 and 60-999, plus the EO 11246 portions of part 60-30), including affirmative action plans and utilization goals, effective 2026-10-26. The Section 503 rule drops the self-identification form and the 7 percent utilization goal and raises the coverage threshold to $20,000; the VEVRAA rule raises its threshold to $200,000.

uncertainties: Law-firm summaries differ on whether effective dates are stated: the Federal Register public-inspection copy gives 2026-10-26 for the EO 11246 rescission, and Crowell, Duane Morris and Honigman summaries give 2026-09-21 for most Section 503 and VEVRAA changes (Crowell, whose summary was also read, is not listed as a source because its publication date was not shown). The OFCCP staff reduction figure (from about 479 to under 50) comes from a law-firm blog and was not checked against DOL. Appropriations figures differ slightly between sources ($100 million to $101 million). Litigation over the final rules was not exhaustively searched; the web search budget ran out after searches on OFCCP and disparate impact only, so most evidence comes from Federal Register queries and fetched pages.
